analysis.investment_thesis: Afcons is the most attractively valued stock in this group on Magic Formula metrics, trading at 10.74x EV/EBITDA (earnings yield ~7-9%) with ROCE of 19.6% approaching the 20% threshold — a near-miss on both criteria rather than a clear failure. However, 4.8% revenue CAGR, finance costs that exceed net profit, and a first-ever negative OCF in FY2025 cap this at a HOLD rather than a buy.
key_strengths: EV/EBITDA of 10.74x and P/S of 0.98x — meaningfully cheaper than peers and the cheapest in this group by Magic Formula metrics
ROCE of 19.6% approaching the 20% Magic Formula threshold, with EBITDA growing 10.5% CAGR over 5 years despite thin sector margins
Specialized expertise in complex infrastructure (marine, metro, tunnels, LNG tanks) creates differentiation vs. generic EPC peers
key_risks: Finance costs of INR 629 Cr in FY25 actually exceed net profit of INR 487 Cr — the interest burden is only covered by INR 469 Cr of 'Other Income' which is non-recurring in nature
Revenue CAGR of only 4.8% over 5 years is sluggish; Magic Formula favors companies where high ROIC compounds through revenue growth
FY2025 OCF turned negative (-INR 132 Cr) for the first time — working capital deterioration in construction projects is a classic warning sign
red_flags: Other Income of INR 469 Cr (27% of EBITDA in FY25) is inflating profitability metrics — strip this out and EBIT coverage of interest costs becomes very thin
Finance costs grew from INR 391 Cr (FY20) to INR 629 Cr (FY25) — borrowings rose to INR 3,565 Cr, materially above reported 'Total Debt' of INR 2,343 Cr
FCF turned to -INR 470 Cr in FY25 after being modestly positive in FY23-24 — capex of INR 344 Cr plus working capital bleed is a concern
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Afcons stands apart from this group because it is the only stock where both Magic Formula metrics are in the same zip code as the required thresholds — earnings yield in the 7–9% range and ROCE at 19.6% vs. the 12% and 20% targets respectively. The EV/EBITDA of 10.74x is also the most reasonable multiple here, and a P/S under 1x signals genuine value relative to business scale. The company has real specialized expertise in technically complex, large-ticket infrastructure projects that not every EPC firm can execute.

The Math on interest coverage, however, is alarming: FY2025 interest costs of INR 629 Cr against EBIT of INR 1,361 Cr gives an interest coverage ratio of ~2.2x before considering Other Income. Stripping the INR 469 Cr of Other Income from EBIT (which includes income from investments and JV profits), core operating earnings cover interest by only 1.4x — far too thin for a construction company exposed to project delays. The negative OCF in FY2025 warrants monitoring. Afcons would cross into BUY territory if earnings yield reaches 12%+ and OCF recovers; at current levels it's a HOLD for existing investors.
